business_problem: EPRI needed to run large reasoning models and AI weather simulations on premises for critical-infrastructure research, but data-sovereignty, compliance, and limited scheduling flexibility made shared remote compute a poor fit for energy-sector workflows.
solution_summary: EPRI built two local AI workflows on NVIDIA deskside systems. Power Chat runs on DGX Spark in a Dell Pro Max with GB10 and serves gpt-oss-120b through the NVIDIA vLLM NGC container with prefix caching, letting researchers load technical documents into a one-million-token cache and ask questions without moving any data outside controlled environments. For operational planning, DGX Station runs AI weather prediction models such as GenCast and NVIDIA FourCastNet and uses NVIDIA CorrDiff and CBottle to downscale climate data into higher-resolution ensemble forecasts. Both workflows are air-gap capable, keep model weights, caches, and inference on premises, and give researchers immediate access to large-scale AI without waiting for shared cluster slots. The result is a sovereign research platform that supports both document analysis and grid-planning forecasts from the same family of local NVIDIA systems.

data_flow: Technical documents are loaded into Power Chat's local cache on DGX Spark for conversational analysis, while gridded weather and climate data is processed on DGX Station through GenCast, FourCastNet, and CorrDiff to produce high-resolution local forecasts for grid planners.
business_outcome: EPRI demonstrated that local AI can serve 35 tokens per second to one researcher and 150 tokens per second across 10 Power Chat users, while a DGX Station GB300 produced a 50-member GenCast ensemble in 150 seconds instead of the 10-plus hours estimated for a CPU server, all without leaving controlled environments.
architecture_clues: Power Chat keeps a one-million-token KV cache resident on one deskside system.
DGX Station stages a 50-member ensemble forecast in a single pass.
Both workflows are air-gap capable with no external network dependency.
